methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $1.7B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Atoms is a Growth-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $1.7B to date. The valuation landscape for this sector includes one public comparable (277810.KQ) and eight private peers, with notable private companies including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. However, the Robotics & Manufacturing peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables at similar valuation tiers to support a robust peer-median analysis—only 10 same-sector companies exist, but none met the threshold of three or more filtered datapoints.

Consequently, valuation relies on the Stage-Progression method, which applies a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of Growth-stage advancement to the $1.7B total raised proxy, yielding an implied value of $2.0B. This method captures the value accretion expected between funding rounds but assumes Atoms' risk and growth profile align with median peers at similar stages.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.7B (floor, tied to total capital deployed) to $2.3B (ceiling), with a median point of $2.0B. Key uncertainties include the lack of narrow-set peer comparables to validate stage-progression assumptions, the absence of disclosed financial metrics, and the broader question of how Atoms' specific market position and unit economics compare to the broader Robotics & Manufacturing cohort. A peer-median analysis becomes viable only with additional private company data or disclosed metrics from comparable growth-stage robotics firms.
